correctness.rationale: The Lindblad equations give z_i(q)=-eta+q(z_i+eta) and b_i(q)=qb_i. In units of h, e_i(q) is the nonnegative upper root of F_i(u)=u^2-2z_i(q)u-qb_i; the other root is nonpositive. For e_1(q)>0, the sign of e_1-e_2 is therefore the sign of F_2(e_1)=q[2(z_1-z_2)e_1+b_1-b_2]. Implicit differentiation gives e_i'=e_i(e_i+2eta)/(2q sqrt(z_i(q)^2+qb_i))>0 on the positive locus. If b_1<b_2, initial ordering forces z_1>z_2 and e_1(1)>e_*>0; as q runs down from 1 to 0 the affine sign changes exactly once, and e_2>0 even if e_1 later vanishes. If b_1>b_2, e_1>0 and the affine sign is positive at both ends of the level range [0,e_1(1)]. For equal b, initial ordering forces z_1>z_2 and monotonicity in z excludes inversion; zero plateaux are not reversals. Substituting the unique level in the quadratic gives the quoted q_* and t_*. With A=2e_*z_1+b_1, q_*(0)=e_*^2/A<1, so dq_*/deta=2e_*(A-e_*^2)/(A+2eta e_*)^2>0, giving the fixed-rate time claim including the bath endpoints. Direct rational substitution for the frozen example gives e_*=7/40, q_*(0)=49/400 and q_*(1)=203/320.
